items.sentence: "We won the lottery!" — "You don't say!"
items.translation: 「我们中彩票了！」——「真的假的！
explanations: **You don't say!** 高语境口语：字面『你不说我也知道』，实际两用——(1) 表惊讶：真的吗！(2) 反讽：谁不知道啊（语气拖长+降调）。
中性场景表惊讶可用 No kidding! / Really? 例：— She quit her job. — You don't say!（她辞职了。——真的假的！）

sentenceAudio.text: "We won the lottery!" — "You don't say!"

items.sentence: The doctor wants to have a second look.
items.translation: 医生想再看一遍（复核一下）。
explanations: **have a second look** = 再看一遍、复核。比 look again 更强调「带着怀疑或求准确的态度再看」，常见于医疗、审稿、验货场景。
近义：take another look / double-check。例句：The editor asked me to have a second look at the opening paragraph.

sentenceAudio.text: The doctor wants to have a second look.

items.sentence: I have to hit the books tonight.
items.translation: 我今晚得啃书本了。
explanations: **hit the books** = 用功读书、啃书本。学生俚语，比 study 更口语，含「下苦功」的劲头。
近义：buckle down（沉下心来）/ cram（考前突击）。例句：Finals are next week, so I'd better hit the books.

sentenceAudio.text: I have to hit the books tonight.

items.sentence: Don't worry, I'm working on it.
items.translation: 别担心，我正在处理。
explanations: **work on it** = 着手处理某事，强调「还在进行中」。常用来回应催促，暗示有进展、别急。
近义：get on it（马上办）/ handle it（搞定它）。区别：work on 强调过程，handle 强调结果。例句：Give me an hour — I'm working on it.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't worry, I'm working on it.

items.sentence: On this team, I have the final say.
items.translation: 在这个团队里，我说了算。
explanations: **have the final say** = 有最终决定权、拍板权。职场高频，强调「最后那一下由谁定」。
近义：have the last word / call the shots。例句：The client has the final say on the design.

sentenceAudio.text: On this team, I have the final say.

items.sentence: I'll keep my eye out for a cheaper flight.
items.translation: 我会留意有没有更便宜的航班。
explanations: **keep an eye out (for)** = 留意、留心看着。语气比 watch 轻，常指顺便帮忙盯着。eye 用单数。
辨析：keep an eye out for 是「找还没出现的」，keep an eye on 是「看着已有的」。例句：Keep an eye out for my package.

sentenceAudio.text: I'll keep my eye out for a cheaper flight.

items.sentence: It was touch and go for a while, but she pulled through.
items.translation: 有一阵子情况危急，但她挺过来了。
chunks: It was touch and go for a while,
explanations: **touch and go** = 情况危急、吉凶未卜，差一点就出事。原指船擦着礁石走，后泛指险情。
**pull through** = 渡过难关、康复过来。例句：The surgery was touch and go, but he pulled through.

sentenceAudio.text: It was touch and go for a while, but she pulled through.

items.sentence: The news was a bombshell.
items.translation: 这个消息如同重磅炸弹。
explanations: **a bombshell** = 爆炸性消息、惊天内幕。多指让人震惊的负面消息（丑闻、突然辞职等）。
搭配：drop a bombshell（抛出重磅消息）。例句：She dropped a bombshell when she announced she was leaving.

sentenceAudio.text: The news was a bombshell.

items.sentence: My boss's attitude is my way or the highway.
items.translation: 我老板的态度是：不听我的就走人。
explanations: **my way or the highway** 字面「走我的路，不然上高速（走人）」，形容独断专行、不容异议。
近义：take it or leave it（爱要不要）。例句：He's a my-way-or-the-highway kind of manager.

sentenceAudio.text: My boss's attitude is my way or the highway.

items.sentence: Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
items.translation: 别高兴太早，蛋还没孵出来呢。
explanations: **Don't count your chickens before they hatch** 谚语：别高兴太早，别指望还没到手的东西。
中文对应「别打如意算盘」「八字还没一撇」。省略版：Don't count your chickens. 例句：The contract isn't signed yet — don't count your chickens.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't count your chickens before they hatch.

items.sentence: She left the party of her own accord.
items.translation: 她主动离开了聚会。
explanations: **of one's own accord** = 自愿地、主动地，没人逼。偏正式书面语，比 by oneself 更强调「出于本人意愿」。
近义：on one's own initiative / voluntarily。例句：He resigned of his own accord.

sentenceAudio.text: She left the party of her own accord.

items.sentence: He's been playing fast and loose with the rules.
items.translation: 他一直在钻规则的空子。
explanations: **play fast and loose (with)** = 玩弄、反复无常、不守规矩。原指街头骗术（飞快挪动赌注），现多指对规则或承诺不认真。
常见搭配对象：the rules / the facts / people's feelings。例句：He played fast and loose with the facts.

sentenceAudio.text: He's been playing fast and loose with the rules.

items.sentence: That deal is robbing Peter to pay Paul.
items.translation: 那笔交易就是拆东墙补西墙。
explanations: **rob Peter to pay Paul** = 拆东墙补西墙，借新债还旧债。字面「抢彼得的钱还给保罗」，源自中世纪教会税制之争。
例句：Taking a new loan to cover the old one is just robbing Peter to pay Paul.

sentenceAudio.text: That deal is robbing Peter to pay Paul.

items.sentence: His remarks rubbed me the wrong way.
items.translation: 他那些话让我听着很不舒服。
explanations: **rub someone the wrong way** = 惹人不快、让人听着别扭。字面「逆着毛摸」，强调说不清缘由的别扭感。
反义：rub someone the right way（讨人喜欢）。例句：His tone rubbed me the wrong way from the start.

sentenceAudio.text: His remarks rubbed me the wrong way.

items.sentence: She is as mild as a dove.
items.translation: 她性情温和得像只鸽子。
explanations: **as mild as a dove** = 像鸽子一样温顺，形容人性格极其柔和、不争不闹。
同结构明喻：as busy as a bee（忙得像蜜蜂）/ as cool as a cucumber（镇定自若）。例句：She's as mild as a dove, but she never backs down on principles.

sentenceAudio.text: She is as mild as a dove.

items.sentence: Thanks for being my rock through all this.
items.translation: 谢谢你在这段艰难里做我的依靠。
explanations: **be someone's rock** = 做某人的靠山、定海神针。指在困难时给人稳定支持的那个人。
可加冠词说 a rock。例句：After the accident, my sister was my rock.

sentenceAudio.text: Thanks for being my rock through all this.

items.sentence: A good seaman is known in bad weather.
items.translation: 好水手要在坏天气里见真章。
hints: 要在恶劣天气里才看得出

grammar.meaning: 在恶劣天气里才看得出来

explanations: **A good seaman is known in bad weather** 谚语：真本事要在困境中见分晓。中文对应「疾风知劲草」。
变体：A good sailor is known in a storm. 例句：He stayed calm when the project crashed — a good seaman is known in bad weather.

sentenceAudio.text: A good seaman is known in bad weather.

items.sentence: You really know your stuff.
items.translation: 你确实很懂行。
explanations: **know one's stuff** = 懂行、业务过硬。称赞别人专业能力时的常见口语表达，stuff 不可数。
近义：know the ropes（懂门道）/ know one's onions（英式俚语）。例句：She's only 25, but she really knows her stuff.

sentenceAudio.text: You really know your stuff.

items.sentence: Don't push me, I'm already at my limit.
items.translation: 别逼我，我已经到极限了。
explanations: **push someone** 在这里不是「推」而是「逼、催到极限」。Don't push me 是划边界的高频口语。
近义：Don't test my patience（别考验我的耐心）。例句：Don't push me — I've had a terrible day.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't push me, I'm already at my limit.

items.sentence: You're impossible, you never listen.
items.translation: 你真不可理喻，从来不听人说话。
explanations: **You're impossible** 口语里不是「你不可能」，而是埋怨人「你真是没治了、没法讲道理」。
语气偏亲昵的抱怨（情侣、家人之间常用），比 you're unreasonable 轻。例句：You're impossible! I give up.

sentenceAudio.text: You're impossible, you never listen.

items.sentence: It's none of your business who I date.
items.translation: 我跟谁约会不关你的事。
explanations: **none of your business** = 不关你的事、少管闲事。语气直接，对陌生人说属冒犯；熟人之间可带玩笑。
委婉版：I'd rather not say. 例句：Who I date is none of your business.

sentenceAudio.text: It's none of your business who I date.

items.sentence: Stop joking, you're killing me!
items.translation: 别逗了，你笑死我了。
explanations: **you're killing me** 不是「你要杀我」，而是夸张口语：笑死我了 / 你太逗了（也可表示被折磨得受不了）。
语境定意：讲笑话时 = 笑死人；被反复催命时 = 你饶了我吧。例句：Stop it, you're killing me!

sentenceAudio.text: Stop joking, you're killing me!

items.sentence: Get over yourself and apologize.
items.translation: 别自我感觉良好了，道个歉吧。
explanations: **get over yourself** = 别自我感觉良好、别太把自己当回事。带责备意味，要对方面对现实。
近义：Get off your high horse（别摆架子）。例句：Get over yourself — not everyone is watching you.

sentenceAudio.text: Get over yourself and apologize.

items.sentence: Don't nag me about the dishes.
items.translation: 别为洗碗的事唠叨我。
explanations: **nag** = 喋喋不休地唠叨、反复挑剔。比 remind（提醒）负面，含「烦人」意味。
近义：nag at / keep on at（英式）。例句：He nags me about the dishes every single night.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't nag me about the dishes.

items.sentence: You're out of line with that comment.
items.translation: 你那句话说得越界了。
explanations: **out of line** = 越界、出格、不合规矩，指言行越过了应有的界限。带批评意味。
反义：in line（守规矩）。例句：His remarks were completely out of line.

sentenceAudio.text: You're out of line with that comment.

items.sentence: I'm sick of it, I quit.
items.translation: 我受够了，不干了。
explanations: **be sick of** = 对某事厌烦透了。语气比 be tired of 更强，接近「忍无可忍」。
近义：be fed up with / be done with。例句：I'm sick of his excuses.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm sick of it, I quit.

items.sentence: Are you all right — you look a little pale.
items.translation: 你还好吗？你脸色有点发白。
explanations: **all right** = 没事、还好。关心他人状态的高频开场，比 Are you okay? 稍正式一点，也常写作 alright。
近义：Are you OK? / Is everything all right? 例句：You fell off your bike — are you all right?

sentenceAudio.text: Are you all right — you look a little pale.

items.sentence: Are you okay — you seem a bit off today.
items.translation: 你还好吧？你今天有点不对劲。
chunks: you seem a bit off today.
explanations: **a bit off** = 有点不对劲、状态不好。off 在这里表示「不寻常、不舒服」，比 sick 委婉，可指身体也可指情绪。
近义：not yourself / a little down。例句：He seems a bit off since he got back from the trip.

sentenceAudio.text: Are you okay — you seem a bit off today.

items.sentence: Don't take it to heart — he was just joking.
items.translation: 别往心里去。他只是开个玩笑。
explanations: **take it to heart** = 把话往心里去、太当真。多用于安慰被批评或被开玩笑的人，否定式 Don't take it to heart 是高频安慰语。
近义：Don't let it get to you. / Don't dwell on it. 例句：His comments were unfair, but don't take them to heart.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't take it to heart — he was just joking.

items.sentence: Whatever happens, I'm here for you.
items.translation: 无论发生什么，我都在你身边。
explanations: **be here for you** = 我在你身边、随时支持你。安慰场景的高频承诺句，强调「不是空话，我人就在」。
近义：I've got your back. / You can count on me. 例句：Losing a job is hard, but remember I'm here for you.

sentenceAudio.text: Whatever happens, I'm here for you.

items.sentence: Is something bothering you — you can tell me.
items.translation: 有什么心事吗？你可以跟我说。
explanations: **bother** = 打扰、使烦恼。Is something bothering you? 比 What's wrong? 更委婉，暗示「我注意到你状态不对」。
近义：Is something on your mind? / Did something happen? 例句：You've been quiet all night — is something bothering you?

sentenceAudio.text: Is something bothering you — you can tell me.

items.sentence: You've been quiet all day — what's on your mind?
items.translation: 你一整天都没说话。你在想什么呢？
explanations: **on one's mind** = 挂在心上、有心事。What's on your mind? 关心的是「在想什么烦心事」，比 What do you think? 更体贴。
区别：take one's mind off（转移注意力）/ keep in mind（记住）。例句：You look worried — what's on your mind?

sentenceAudio.text: You've been quiet all day — what's on your mind?

items.sentence: Look on the bright side — nobody got hurt.
items.translation: 往好处想嘛。没有人受伤。
explanations: **look on the bright side** = 往好处想、看到积极一面。安慰翻车现场的标准句，常接 but/nobody 引出「万幸」。
近义：Every cloud has a silver lining. 例句：We lost the game, but look on the bright side — we played as a team.

sentenceAudio.text: Look on the bright side — nobody got hurt.

items.sentence: You remembered my birthday — that's so sweet!
items.translation: 你记得我的生日。太贴心了！
explanations: **That's so sweet!** = 太贴心了、好暖心。回应别人的细心举动，sweet 在口语里指「体贴暖心」，不是「甜」。
近义：That's so thoughtful of you. / You're so kind. 例句：He brought me soup when I was sick. That's so sweet!

sentenceAudio.text: You remembered my birthday — that's so sweet!

items.sentence: Don't worry — we'll get through this together.
items.translation: 别担心。我们会一起挺过去的。
explanations: **get through** = 挺过、熬过（难关）。get through this 强调「这段困难会过去」，加 together 是给对方打气的力量感。
近义：pull through（挺过来，多指病痛）/ ride it out。例句：Money is tight this month, but we'll get through this together.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't worry — we'll get through this together.

items.sentence: Everyone ran out of the building — what's going on?
items.translation: 大家都跑出了大楼。发生什么事了？
chunks: Everyone ran out of the building —
explanations: **go on** = 发生。What's going on? 是询问现场情况的万能句，比 What happened? 更强调「此刻正在进行」。
近义：What's happening? / What's the matter? 例句：Why is everyone gathered here? What's going on?

sentenceAudio.text: Everyone ran out of the building — what's going on?

items.sentence: You've been sighing all morning — what's wrong?
items.translation: 你一早上都在叹气。怎么了？
explanations: **What's wrong?** = 怎么了、出什么事了。最直接的关心句，wrong 指「有问题、不对劲」，语气比 What's going on? 更私人。
近义：What's the matter? / Is something wrong? 例句：You look upset. What's wrong?

sentenceAudio.text: You've been sighing all morning — what's wrong?

items.sentence: You're not yourself today — is everything fine at home?
items.translation: 你今天不太对劲。家里一切都好吗？
explanations: **not oneself** = 不对劲、不像平时的自己。指情绪或状态明显反常，是委婉关心的经典句式。
近义：You seem a bit off. / You're acting strange today. 例句：You've hardly eaten anything — you're not yourself today.

sentenceAudio.text: You're not yourself today — is everything fine at home?

items.sentence: Just to be clear, the deadline is Friday, not Monday.
items.translation: 先说清楚，截止日期是周五，不是周一。
chunks: the deadline is Friday, not Monday.
hints: 截止日期是周五不是周一

grammar.meaning: 截止日期是周五不是周一

explanations: **just to be clear** = 先说清楚、确认一下。职场高频开场，用于消除歧义，比 to be honest 语气更中性。
近义：To be clear / Just so we're on the same page. 例句：Just to be clear, this discount applies today only.

sentenceAudio.text: Just to be clear, the deadline is Friday, not Monday.

items.sentence: He always promises a lot, if you know what I mean.
items.translation: 他总是许下很多承诺，你懂我意思吧。
chunks: if you know what I mean.
explanations: **you know what I mean** = 你懂我意思吧。暗示「话里有话，不便挑明」，口语里常缩略成 you know what I'm saying / know what I mean?
近义：if you catch my drift. / you get me? 例句：He's generous with words, if you know what I mean.

sentenceAudio.text: He always promises a lot, if you know what I mean.

items.sentence: You really got me the tickets — do you mean it?
items.translation: 你真的给我搞到票了？你是认真的吗？
chunks: You really got me the tickets —
explanations: **mean it** = 说真的、不是开玩笑。Do you mean it? 用于确认对方的话是真心还是随口一说，惊喜或怀疑时都用。
近义：Are you serious? / Really? 例句：You're giving me your old laptop? Do you mean it?

sentenceAudio.text: You really got me the tickets — do you mean it?

items.sentence: The bill looks wrong — it doesn't make sense.
items.translation: 这账单看着不对。完全说不通。
explanations: **make sense** = 说得通、有道理。否定式 doesn't make sense 表示「逻辑上讲不通」，质疑账单、规则、解释时都用它。
近义：That doesn't add up. 例句：The math is right, but the answer still doesn't make sense.

sentenceAudio.text: The bill looks wrong — it doesn't make sense.

items.sentence: Thanks for the warning — i'll take a raincoat with me.
items.translation: 谢谢提醒。我会带件雨衣。
chunks: i'll take a raincoat with me.
explanations: **thanks for the warning** = 谢谢提醒。回应别人好意告知风险，比 thanks for telling me 更明确指向「预警」。
近义：Good to know. / I appreciate the heads-up. 例句：Thanks for the warning — I'll avoid that road at night.

sentenceAudio.text: Thanks for the warning — i'll take a raincoat with me.

items.sentence: Watch out — there's a step behind you.
items.translation: 小心！你身后有一级台阶。
explanations: **watch out** = 小心、当心。紧急提醒的高频短语动词，比 be careful 更急迫，常单独喊出来。
近义：Look out! / Mind the step. 例句：Watch out! The floor is wet.

sentenceAudio.text: Watch out — there's a step behind you.

items.sentence: To make a long story short, we missed the last train.
items.translation: 长话短说，我们错过了末班车。
chunks: To make a long story short,
explanations: **make a long story short** = 长话短说。讲述冗长经历前先给结论，口语也常用短版 long story short。
近义：To cut a long story short（英式）/ bottom line。例句：To make a long story short, we got lost and arrived an hour late.

sentenceAudio.text: To make a long story short, we missed the last train.

items.sentence: I only have five minutes, so please make it brief.
items.translation: 我只有五分钟，请说得简短些。
explanations: **make it brief** = 说得简短些。职场会议高频，brief 作形容词指「简明扼要」，it 指你要说的内容。
近义：Keep it short. / Get to the point. 例句：The boss is busy — make it brief.

sentenceAudio.text: I only have five minutes, so please make it brief.

items.sentence: Stop beating around the bush and come to the point.
items.translation: 别绕弯子了，直说重点吧。
explanations: **beat around the bush** = 拐弯抹角、绕弯子。源自狩猎时用棍子打灌木赶猎物，引申为「不直入正题」。
**come to the point** = 直说重点。与前者是一对反义搭配，常连用催对方进入正题。例句：Stop beating around the bush and come to the point.

sentenceAudio.text: Stop beating around the bush and come to the point.

items.sentence: Open the door, please — it's urgent!
items.translation: 请开门！事情很紧急！
explanations: **urgent** = 紧急的、十万火急。指需要立刻处理，医疗、工作、快递场景通用，语气比 important 强得多。
近义：It can't wait. / It's an emergency. 例句：Sorry to call so late, but it's urgent.

sentenceAudio.text: Open the door, please — it's urgent!

items.sentence: I'm still learning English, so could you speak slower?
items.translation: 我还在学英语，所以您能说慢一点吗？
explanations: **Could you speak slower?** = 能说慢一点吗？Could 比 Can 更客气；更礼貌的版本是 Could you speak more slowly, please?
近义：Could you slow down a little? 例句：Could you speak slower? English isn't my first language.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm still learning English, so could you speak slower?

items.sentence: I need your advice, so do you have a second?
items.translation: 我需要你的建议，所以你有空吗？
chunks: so do you have a second?
explanations: **have a second** = 有一小会儿空。second 这里指「片刻」，比 have time 更轻量，暗示「很快就好」。
近义：Do you have a minute? / Got a sec? 例句：Do you have a second? I want to run something by you.

sentenceAudio.text: I need your advice, so do you have a second?

items.sentence: I set the table, so it's your turn to do the dishes.
items.translation: 我摆好了餐具，所以轮到你洗碗了。
chunks: so it's your turn to do the dishes.
explanations: **it's your turn to do sth** = 轮到你做某事了。turn 表示「轮流的机会」，家庭分工、游戏排队都靠它。
近义：You're up. / Over to you. 例句：I cooked dinner, so it's your turn to wash up.

sentenceAudio.text: I set the table, so it's your turn to do the dishes.

items.sentence: Please keep an eye on it — I'll be back in ten minutes.
items.translation: 你能帮我看着点吗？我十分钟后回来。
chunks: Please keep an eye on it —
I'll be back in ten minutes.
explanations: **keep an eye on** = 照看、留意。eye 用单数是习惯用法，指「持续盯着」，托人看包、看孩子、看锅都用它。
区别：keep an eye out for（留意寻找某物）。例句：Keep an eye on my bag while I buy tickets.

sentenceAudio.text: Please keep an eye on it — I'll be back in ten minutes.

items.sentence: If I sound rude, I don't mean it.
items.translation: 如果我听起来很粗鲁，我不是故意的。
explanations: **mean it** = 当真的、故意的。否定式 I don't mean it 是道歉高频句，表示「话出口但不是那个意思」。
近义：I didn't mean that. / No offense intended. 例句：Sorry if I hurt your feelings — I don't mean it.

sentenceAudio.text: If I sound rude, I don't mean it.

items.sentence: I forgot our anniversary — I feel really bad.
items.translation: 我忘了我们的纪念日，感觉糟透了。
explanations: **feel really bad** = 感到非常过意不去。bad 在这里指「内疚」，不是身体难受；比 sorry 更强调自责的情绪。
近义：I feel terrible about it. / I feel so guilty. 例句：I snapped at you earlier — I feel really bad.

sentenceAudio.text: I forgot our anniversary — I feel really bad.

items.sentence: The files got deleted — it's all my fault.
items.translation: 文件被删掉了，全怪我。
explanations: **it's all my fault** = 全是我的错。主动揽责的标准句，all 加强「一个都赖不掉」的语气。
近义：I'm entirely to blame. / My bad.（更随意）。反问版：How is it my fault? 例句：Don't blame the intern — it's all my fault.

sentenceAudio.text: The files got deleted — it's all my fault.

items.sentence: It's Thursday, not Wednesday — my mistake.
items.translation: 是周四不是周三，我搞错了。
explanations: **my mistake** = 我的错、我搞错了。认错的最短版本，多用于纠正事实性错误（记错时间、看错名单），语气轻。
近义：My bad.（更口语）/ Sorry, I got it wrong. 例句：The meeting is at three? My mistake — it's at four.

sentenceAudio.text: It's Thursday, not Wednesday — my mistake.

items.sentence: I lost the tickets — this is my fault.
items.translation: 我把票弄丢了，这是我的错。
explanations: **this is my fault** = 这是我的错。比 it's my fault 更具体指向「眼前这件事」，认错时指明责任归属。
区别：it's all my fault（全是我的错，揽全部）/ it's partly my fault（部分是我的错）。例句：We missed the exit because I was talking — this is my fault.

sentenceAudio.text: I lost the tickets — this is my fault.

items.sentence: The launch failed, and I take full responsibility.
items.translation: 发布失败了，我承担全部责任。
explanations: **take full responsibility** = 承担全部责任。正式度最高的揽责句，职场、公开声明通用，比 sorry 更有担当感。
近义：I'm accountable for this. / The buck stops with me. 例句：The shipment was late, and I take full responsibility.

sentenceAudio.text: The launch failed, and I take full responsibility.

items.sentence: I'm awful sorry about the noise last night.
items.translation: 昨晚吵到你了，实在抱歉。
explanations: **awful sorry** = 非常抱歉。awful 在这里是「非常」的口语强化词（不是「糟糕」），美国南方口语尤其常见，相当于 terribly sorry。
近义：terribly sorry / awfully sorry。例句：I'm awful sorry to trouble you again.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm awful sorry about the noise last night.

items.sentence: I'm sorry about this mess in the kitchen.
items.translation: 厨房乱成这样，很抱歉。
chunks: about this mess in the kitchen.
explanations: **sorry about...** = 为……抱歉。about 后接具体事物，比 sorry for 更口语；mess 指乱七八糟的状态。
近义：Sorry for the mess. / Excuse the mess. 例句：Come on in — sorry about the mess.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm sorry about this mess in the kitchen.

items.sentence: Sorry to keep you waiting — the traffic was terrible.
items.translation: 让你久等了，路上太堵了。
explanations: **keep you waiting** = 让你一直等。Sorry to keep you waiting 是迟到标准开场，比 Sorry I'm late 多一层「我知道你在等」的体谅。
近义：Sorry for the delay. / Sorry I'm late. 例句：Sorry to keep you waiting — the meeting ran over.

sentenceAudio.text: Sorry to keep you waiting — the traffic was terrible.

items.sentence: Sorry to barge in — is this seat taken?
items.translation: 冒昧打扰了，这个座位有人吗？
explanations: **barge in** = 闯入、贸然打断。barge 本义是「横冲直撞」，barge in 带自知理亏的劲儿，道歉时用很自然。
近义：Sorry to interrupt. / Sorry to crash in on you. 例句：Sorry to barge in while you're eating.

sentenceAudio.text: Sorry to barge in — is this seat taken?

items.sentence: My apologies for the late reply.
items.translation: 回复晚了，非常抱歉。
explanations: **my apologies** = 我深表歉意。名词化的道歉，比 I'm sorry 正式，邮件、职场高频；apology 用复数表示诚意。
近义：Please accept my apologies. / My sincere apologies. 例句：My apologies for missing the call — I was in a tunnel.

sentenceAudio.text: My apologies for the late reply.

items.sentence: I sincerely apologize for what I said yesterday.
items.translation: 我为我昨天说的话诚恳道歉。
explanations: **sincerely apologize** = 诚恳道歉。sincerely（真诚地）是道歉的强度词，正式场合或真心伤到人时用。
近义：I owe you an apology. / I sincerely regret it. 例句：I sincerely apologize for the confusion my email caused.

sentenceAudio.text: I sincerely apologize for what I said yesterday.

items.sentence: I shouldn't have shouted at you — do you forgive me?
items.translation: 我不该冲你吼，你能原谅我吗？
chunks: I shouldn't have shouted at you —
explanations: **shouldn't have done** = 本不该做（却做了）。表对过去的自责，道歉时先认错再求原谅，是很诚恳的句式。
近义：I was out of line. / Can you ever forgive me?（更重）。例句：I shouldn't have said that — please forgive me.

sentenceAudio.text: I shouldn't have shouted at you — do you forgive me?

items.sentence: You stepped on his foot — say you're sorry.
items.translation: 你踩到他的脚了，快说对不起。
explanations: **say you're sorry** = 说声对不起。大人催小孩道歉的经典句，对成年人用会带命令甚至讽刺味，注意场景。
近义：Apologize to him. / Say sorry right now. 例句：You took her toy — say you're sorry.

sentenceAudio.text: You stepped on his foot — say you're sorry.

items.sentence: Don't pout — I'll buy you an ice cream.
items.translation: 别撅嘴了，我给你买冰淇淋。
chunks: I'll buy you an ice cream.
explanations: **pout** = 撅嘴、闹别扭。指不满时嘟起嘴的样子，孩子和撒娇的恋人都常用，Don't pout 带哄人的语气。
近义：Don't sulk.（闷闷不乐）/ Don't give me that look. 例句：Don't pout — we'll go to the park tomorrow.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't pout — I'll buy you an ice cream.

items.sentence: Don't mention it — it's my pleasure.
items.translation: 别客气，帮你是我的荣幸。
explanations: **don't mention it** = 别客气、不值一提。回应感谢的经典句，意思是「这点小事别放嘴上」。
**it's my pleasure** = 我的荣幸。比 don't mention it 更热情，服务行业、朋友间通用，也可单说 My pleasure.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't mention it — it's my pleasure.

items.sentence: Your help is greatly appreciated.
items.translation: 十分感谢你的帮助。
explanations: **(much/greatly) appreciated** = 不胜感激。被动式致谢，邮件、正式场合高频；口语缩略成 Much appreciated.
近义：Thank you so much. / I'm very grateful. 例句：Your prompt reply is much appreciated.

sentenceAudio.text: Your help is greatly appreciated.

items.sentence: I'm truly grateful for your help with the report.
items.translation: 你帮我做报告，我真心感激。
chunks: for your help with the report.

grammar.meaning: 对你帮忙做报告这件事

explanations: **be grateful for sth** = 为某事感激。grateful 比 thank you 更走心，强调「记在心里」的感激。
近义：I can't thank you enough. / I owe you one. 例句：I'm truly grateful for your support this year.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm truly grateful for your help with the report.

items.sentence: You fixed my bike so fast — I really appreciate it.
items.translation: 你这么快就修好了我的自行车，我真的很感激。
chunks: You fixed my bike so fast —
hints: 你这么快就修好了我的自行车
explanations: **I really appreciate it** = 我真的很感激。最通用的口头致谢升级版，比 thank you 更有分量，it 指对方做的整件事。
近义：Thanks a million. / I can't thank you enough. 例句：You watered my plants all week? I really appreciate it.

sentenceAudio.text: You fixed my bike so fast — I really appreciate it.

items.sentence: You covered my shift yesterday — I owe you bigtime!
items.translation: 你昨天替我值班，我欠你个大人情！
explanations: **owe you bigtime** = 大大欠你个人情。bigtime 是口语副词「大大地、非常」，比 I owe you one 的分量重得多。
近义：I owe you one. / I'm in your debt. 例句：You talked to the landlord for me? I owe you bigtime!

sentenceAudio.text: You covered my shift yesterday — I owe you bigtime!

items.sentence: The manager praised our report — keep up the good work.
items.translation: 经理表扬了我们的报告，再接再厉啊。
hints: 经理表扬了我们的报告

grammar.meaning: 经理表扬了我们的报告

explanations: **keep up the good work** = 再接再厉、保持佳绩。夸人+鼓励的标准收尾句，邮件评价、老师批语通用。
近义：Keep it up! / Way to go! 例句：Sales are up this quarter — keep up the good work.

sentenceAudio.text: The manager praised our report — keep up the good work.

items.sentence: I'm counting on you — don't let me down.
items.translation: 我就指望你了，别让我失望。
explanations: **count on** = 指望、依靠。I'm counting on you 是把事交出去前的信任宣言，常接 don't let me down 加压。
**let sb down** = 让某人失望。let down 是「放鸽子/掉链子」的通感表达，否定的 don't let me down 是托付标配。例句：This presentation matters — I'm counting on you, don't let me down.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm counting on you — don't let me down.

items.sentence: Are you free this Saturday for a movie?
items.translation: 这周六你有空看电影吗？
explanations: **be free** = 有空。约人最常用的问法，比 Do you have time 更轻松；free 后直接接时间即可。
近义：Are you available?（更正式）/ Got any plans Saturday? 例句：Are you free tonight? I'd love to grab dinner.

sentenceAudio.text: Are you free this Saturday for a movie?

items.sentence: She has a crush on her coworker.
items.translation: 她对一位同事有意思。
explanations: **have a crush on sb** = 暗恋、对某人有好感。crush 本义「压碎」，转指「心动得心跳加速」，多指还没表白的那种喜欢。
近义：be into sb（更口语）/ have feelings for sb。例句：He's had a crush on her since high school.

sentenceAudio.text: She has a crush on her coworker.

items.sentence: I can't live without you.
items.translation: 我不能没有你。
explanations: **can't live without you** = 不能没有你。最直白的深情表达，恋人常用；也可戏谑用于咖啡、手机等离不开的东西。
近义：You mean the world to me. 例句：You're my whole world — I can't live without you.

sentenceAudio.text: I can't live without you.

items.sentence: Don't be jealous — I only have eyes for you.
items.translation: 别吃醋，我眼里只有你。
chunks: I only have eyes for you.
explanations: **only have eyes for sb** = 眼里只有某人。用「眼睛」表达专一，比 I love only you 更含蓄浪漫。
近义：You're the only one for me. / I'm all yours. 例句：She's beautiful, but I only have eyes for you.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't be jealous — I only have eyes for you.

items.sentence: It's getting late — I'll take you home.
items.translation: 天不早了，我送你回家。
explanations: **take sb home** = 送某人回家（自己开车/陪同）。对比 walk sb home（走回去）、drive sb home（开车送），take 最通用。
近义：Let me see you home. / I'll give you a ride home. 例句：It's raining — I'll take you home.

sentenceAudio.text: It's getting late — I'll take you home.

items.sentence: Honestly, I'm quite fond of you.
items.translation: 老实说，我挺喜欢你的。
explanations: **be fond of sb** = 喜欢某人。比 like 更含蓄稳重，多用于「日久生情」的温和好感，语气不冲。
近义：I have a soft spot for you. / I've grown to like you。例句：I'm very fond of my old professor.

sentenceAudio.text: Honestly, I'm quite fond of you.

items.sentence: I'm driving past your place — I'll drop you off.
items.translation: 我正好路过你那儿，顺路送你。

grammar.meaning: 我正开车路过你住的地方

explanations: **drop sb off** = 顺路把某人送到（某地）。开车场景高频，指「到了就放下人」，宾语放中间 drop me off。
区别：pick sb up（去接人）/ see sb off（送别）。例句：I'll drop you off at the station on my way.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm driving past your place — I'll drop you off.

items.sentence: Put your wallet away — it's on me.
items.translation: 把钱包收起来，这顿我请。
explanations: **it's on me** = 我请客、算我的。on 表示「由谁承担费用」，也可换人称 it's on the house（店里免费）。
近义：This one's on me. / I've got this. / It's my treat. 例句：You paid last time — dinner is on me tonight.

sentenceAudio.text: Put your wallet away — it's on me.

items.sentence: You are adorable when you laugh.
items.translation: 你笑起来真可爱。
explanations: **adorable** = 可爱得让人心动。比 cute 更强烈、更带宠溺感，夸人时常指「让人忍不住喜欢」。
近义：You're so cute. / You're charming. 例句：Look at that baby — she's adorable.

sentenceAudio.text: You are adorable when you laugh.

items.sentence: You take my breath away every time you smile.
items.translation: 你每次微笑都让我屏住呼吸。
explanations: **take sb's breath away** = 让某人惊艳到失语。意象：美得让人忘了呼吸，是最高级的赞美之一。
近义：You leave me speechless. / You're stunning. 例句：The view from the top took my breath away.

sentenceAudio.text: You take my breath away every time you smile.

items.sentence: Your timing is just right — I just finished cooking.
items.translation: 你来得正好，我刚做好饭。
explanations: **timing is just right** = 时机正好、来得巧。timing 指「时间上的把握」，just right 强调分毫不差。
反义：bad timing（来得不是时候）。例句：Perfect timing — dinner is ready.

sentenceAudio.text: Your timing is just right — I just finished cooking.

items.sentence: You look tired — I'll leave you be.
items.translation: 你看起来很累，我就不打扰了。
explanations: **leave sb be** = 不去打扰某人、让某人清静。比 leave sb alone 更温和，含「体谅对方需要空间」的意味。
近义：I'll let you rest. / I'll get out of your hair. 例句：You've had a long day — I'll leave you be.

sentenceAudio.text: You look tired — I'll leave you be.

items.sentence: One more try — you can do it!
items.translation: 再试一次，你能行的！
explanations: **you can do it** = 你能做到。最普及的打气句，简短的三个词自带力量，比赛、考试、健身都用。
近义：You've got this. / Hang in there. 例句：Only one lap left — you can do it!

sentenceAudio.text: One more try — you can do it!

items.sentence: I'm flattered, but I can't accept.
items.translation: 我受宠若惊，但我不能接受。
explanations: **I'm flattered** = 我受宠若惊、过奖了。被夸奖或被邀请时的礼貌回应，为之后的婉拒做铺垫，非常得体。
用法：可单用回谢夸奖（= 太抬举我了），也可像本句接 but 引出拒绝。例句：That's a generous offer, and I'm flattered.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm flattered, but I can't accept.

items.sentence: I admire you for speaking up at the meeting.
items.translation: 我佩服你敢在会上开口。
chunks: for speaking up at the meeting.
explanations: **admire sb for sth** = 因某事佩服某人。admire 是「由衷敬佩」，比 respect 更带感情，for 后接令人佩服的原因。
近义：I look up to you. / I really respect you for that. 例句：I admire her for standing by her decision.

sentenceAudio.text: I admire you for speaking up at the meeting.

items.sentence: You aced the exam — you are awesome!
items.translation: 你考试拿了高分，你太棒了！
explanations: **ace sth** = 在某事上拿满分、做得极漂亮。源自扑克牌 A（ace 最高牌），可接 exam / interview / test。
**You are awesome** = 你太棒了。awesome 在口语里是「超厉害」，比 great 情绪更强。例句：She aced the presentation — everyone clapped.

sentenceAudio.text: You aced the exam — you are awesome!

items.sentence: You are one in a million — never change.
items.translation: 你是万里挑一的人，别变。
chunks: You are one in a million —
explanations: **one in a million** = 万里挑一、独一无二。用概率表达稀有，是赞美别人特别之处的常用句。
近义：You're one of a kind. / There's no one like you. 例句：Thanks for always helping me — you're one in a million.

sentenceAudio.text: You are one in a million — never change.

items.sentence: You passed the driving test — you did it!
items.translation: 你驾照考过了，你做到了！
explanations: **you did it** = 你做到了。见证对方努力后成功的欢呼句，比 congratulations 更直接带情绪。
近义：You made it! / Well done! 例句：After three attempts, you did it!

sentenceAudio.text: You passed the driving test — you did it!

items.sentence: You got us front-row seats — you are the man!
items.translation: 你给我们弄到了前排座位，你太厉害了！

grammar.meaning: 你给我们弄到了前排座位

explanations: **you are the man** = 你太厉害了、你是大哥。男性间的高强度赞美（对女性可说 you're the best），感谢对方帮了大忙。
近义：You're the best. / You rock. 例句：You fixed my laptop in ten minutes — you are the man!

sentenceAudio.text: You got us front-row seats — you are the man!

items.sentence: You made me breakfast in bed — you are so sweet.
items.translation: 你给我做了早餐，还送到床上，你太贴心了。
chunks: You made me breakfast in bed —
hints: 你给我做了早餐，还送到床上

grammar.meaning: 你给我做了早餐，还送到床上

explanations: **breakfast in bed** = 送到床上享用的早餐。情侣、家人之间的甜蜜仪式感表达，固定搭配不加冠词。
**you are so sweet** = 你太贴心了。sweet 形容人「温柔体贴」，注意不是「甜」。例句：Thanks for the surprise — you are so sweet.

sentenceAudio.text: You made me breakfast in bed — you are so sweet.

items.sentence: Take it easy at the gym — don't overdo it.
items.translation: 在健身房悠着点，别练过头。
chunks: Take it easy at the gym —
explanations: **overdo it** = 做得过头、用力过猛。适用于运动、喝酒、加班——凡事超出身体能承受的度。
近义：Don't push yourself too hard. / Take it slow. 例句：You just recovered — don't overdo it.

sentenceAudio.text: Take it easy at the gym — don't overdo it.

items.sentence: Information came in by dribs and drabs.
items.translation: 消息零零散散地传了过来。
explanations: **by dribs and drabs** = 零零星星、一点一点地。强调「不成批、不连续」，常形容消息、捐款、人流慢慢来。
近义：in bits and pieces / little by little。例句：The donations came in by dribs and drabs.

sentenceAudio.text: Information came in by dribs and drabs.

items.sentence: Free concert tickets — you're pulling my leg!
items.translation: 免费演唱会门票，你在逗我吧！
explanations: **pull sb's leg** = 逗某人、拿某人开玩笑。不是「拉腿」！指善意地哄骗逗趣，常用来表示「我不信，你在骗我」。
近义：You're kidding me. / You're teasing me. 例句：Seriously, I'm not pulling your leg — the tickets are real.

sentenceAudio.text: Free concert tickets — you're pulling my leg!

items.sentence: It's your first week, so ease into it.
items.translation: 这是你的第一周，慢慢上手吧。
explanations: **ease into sth** = 慢慢进入状态、渐进适应。ease 是「缓和」，比 start 多一层「别急、慢来」的劝告语气。
近义：take it slow / get into the swing of it。例句：New job? Give yourself a month to ease into it.

sentenceAudio.text: It's your first week, so ease into it.

items.sentence: It's just a small injection — don't be a baby.
items.translation: 只是打个小针，别像个小孩一样。
explanations: **don't be a baby** = 别像个小孩似的、别娇气。哄小孩或略带嫌弃地劝人别闹，对成年人说会显得不太客气。
近义：Don't be such a wimp. / Be a big boy. 例句：It's only a splinter — don't be a baby.

sentenceAudio.text: It's just a small injection — don't be a baby.

items.sentence: You can't fool me — I have your number.
items.translation: 你骗不了我，我早就看透你了。
explanations: **have sb's number** = 摸清某人的底、看透某人。不是「有电话号码」！指知道对方真实动机，不被花招骗到。
近义：I've got you figured out. / I know your game. 例句：Nice try, but I have your number.

sentenceAudio.text: You can't fool me — I have your number.

items.sentence: You lied to my face — you have a lot of nerve!
items.translation: 你当面骗我，你居然还有脸！
chunks: you have a lot of nerve!
explanations: **have a lot of nerve** = 脸皮真厚、胆子真大。指责对方「居然敢这么做」，语气强烈；也说 have some nerve。
近义：How dare you! / You've got some guts. 例句：You asked me for a raise after that mess — you have a lot of nerve.

sentenceAudio.text: You lied to my face — you have a lot of nerve!

items.sentence: Stop it — that's not funny.
items.translation: 住手，这一点都不好笑。
explanations: **stop it** = 住手、别闹了。制止正在发生的动作，语气直接；比单说 Stop 更聚焦「这件事」。
近义：Cut it out（更口语、带不耐烦）/ Knock it off。例句：Stop it — you're going to break something.

sentenceAudio.text: Stop it — that's not funny.

items.sentence: Stop that right now!
items.translation: 马上给我停下！
explanations: **stop that** = 停下那个（动作）。that 指对方手上的动作，比 it 更强调「就是你正在干的那事」。
**right now** 放句末是加重语气的催促。近义：Stop that this instant!（更严厉）例句：Stop that right now — I won't say it again.

sentenceAudio.text: Stop that right now!

items.sentence: Stop him — he's getting away!
items.translation: 拦住他，他要跑了！
explanations: **stop sb** = 拦住某人、让某人停下。stop 接人表示阻止某人，接事（stop it）表示让某事停止。
**get away** = 逃脱、溜走。例句：Stop him — he's getting away with my bag!

sentenceAudio.text: Stop him — he's getting away!

items.sentence: Don't touch me — I mean it!
items.translation: 别碰我，我说真的！
explanations: **Don't touch me** 是最直接的肢体边界表达，语气强硬，不留余地。
**I mean it** = 我不是开玩笑，用来给前面的话加重。近义：Keep your hands off me。例句：Don't touch me — I mean it, back off.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't touch me — I mean it!

items.sentence: Get your hands off me!
items.translation: 把你的手拿开！
explanations: **get one's hands off sb** = 把手从某人身上拿开。被拉扯、被冒犯时的强硬抗议。
近义：Take your hands off me! / Hands off!（更短更冲）例句：Get your hands off me — who do you think you are?

sentenceAudio.text: Get your hands off me!

items.sentence: Please line up, everyone.
items.translation: 请大家排好队。
explanations: **line up** = 排队。英式美式通用，最常用的排队说法。
近义：queue up（英式）/ get in line（美式）。例句：Please line up, everyone — the doors are about to open.

sentenceAudio.text: Please line up, everyone.

items.sentence: Please form a line at the door.
items.translation: 请在门口排成一列。
explanations: **form a line** = 排成一列。比 line up 更正式，多用于广播、场馆、机场的指令。
近义：form a queue（英式正式）。例句：Please form a line at the door and have your tickets ready.

sentenceAudio.text: Please form a line at the door.

items.sentence: Don't cut in line — go to the back.
items.translation: 别插队，到后面去。
explanations: **cut in line** = 插队（美式）。英式说 jump the queue；cut in 本身有「插进来」的意思。
近义：jump the queue（英式）/ butt in line。例句：Excuse me, you can't cut in line — go to the back.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't cut in line — go to the back.

items.sentence: Get in line and wait your turn.
items.translation: 排队去，按顺序等着。
explanations: **get in line** = 排队（美式口语），比 line up 更随意。
**wait your turn** = 等着轮到你。强调按顺序来、别抢。例句：Get in line and wait your turn like everyone else.

sentenceAudio.text: Get in line and wait your turn.

items.sentence: Don't shove — there's room for everyone.
items.translation: 别推挤，位置够所有人站。
explanations: **shove** = 用手肘或身体硬推。比 push 更粗鲁，专指人群里乱挤。
近义：Don't push（一般推挤）/ Stop shoving。例句：Don't shove — there's room for everyone on the bus.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't shove — there's room for everyone.

items.sentence: Stand back — the train is coming.
items.translation: 退后，列车要来了。
explanations: **stand back** = 退后、站远一点。安全提示高频，比 move back 更强调保持距离。
近义：Keep back / Stay clear。例句：Stand back — the train is coming and the platform is slippery.

sentenceAudio.text: Stand back — the train is coming.

items.sentence: Stay down and don't move!
items.translation: 趴下别动！
explanations: **stay down** = 保持低位、别起身。多用于危险或紧急场景里的指令。
近义：Get down and stay down。例句：Stay down and don't move until I say it's clear.

sentenceAudio.text: Stay down and don't move!

items.sentence: Stay away from me.
items.translation: 离我远点。
explanations: **stay away from sb** = 跟某人保持距离。划清界限的警告，语气冷静但强硬。
近义：Keep away from me / Keep your distance。例句：Stay away from me — I don't want to talk to you.

sentenceAudio.text: Stay away from me.

items.sentence: Get away from me!
items.translation: 滚开，别靠近我！
explanations: **get away from sb** = 从某人身边走开。比 stay away 更冲，带即时驱赶的怒气。
近义：Back off! / Get lost!（更粗鲁）例句：Get away from me — don't you dare touch my phone!

sentenceAudio.text: Get away from me!

items.sentence: Go away — I need to be alone.
items.translation: 走开，我想一个人待着。
explanations: **go away** = 走开、离开。最常见的驱赶表达，轻重完全看语调。
近义：Leave me alone（别烦我）/ Get out。例句：Go away — I need to be alone for a while.

sentenceAudio.text: Go away — I need to be alone.

items.sentence: Get out of here!
items.translation: 滚出去！

grammar.pos: 驱赶对方离开的口语表达

explanations: **get out of here** = 出去、滚出去。字面是「离开这里」；口语里也能表惊讶，相当于「别逗了」。
近义：Get lost! / Out! 例句：Get out of here — you're not welcome anymore.

sentenceAudio.text: Get out of here!

items.sentence: Keep it out of sight.
items.translation: 把它藏好别让人看见。

grammar.meaning: out of sight 在视线之外

explanations: **out of sight** = 在视线之外、看不见。keep sth out of sight 就是把某物收好、别露出来。
反义：in sight（在看得见的地方）。例句：Keep it out of sight — the guards are checking bags.

sentenceAudio.text: Keep it out of sight.

items.sentence: Don't blab this to anyone.
items.translation: 这事别跟任何人乱说。
explanations: **blab** = 嘴不牢、到处乱说。含贬义，专指把该保密的事说漏出去。
近义：Don't spill the beans / Keep it to yourself。例句：Don't blab this to anyone — it's not official yet.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't blab this to anyone.

items.sentence: No tricks — just tell me the truth.
items.translation: 别耍花样，说实话。
explanations: **no tricks** = 不许耍花样、别玩手段。No + 名词构成简短禁令，语气干脆。
近义：No games / No funny business。例句：No tricks — just tell me the truth and we'll be fine.

sentenceAudio.text: No tricks — just tell me the truth.

items.sentence: Don't call me names!
items.translation: 别骂我！

grammar.pos: call someone names 的否定祈使句
grammar.meaning: 别辱骂我；别给我起侮辱性绰号

explanations: **call sb names** = 骂人、给人起侮辱性绰号。注意必须用复数 names，单数没有这个意思。
近义：Don't insult me / Stop name-calling。例句：Don't call me names — argue with facts, not insults.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't call me names!

items.sentence: Take it or leave it.
items.translation: 要就要，不要拉倒。
explanations: **take it or leave it** = 要就要、不要拉倒。谈判里下最后通牒，表示没有商量余地。
近义：It's my final offer。例句：That's the price — take it or leave it.

sentenceAudio.text: Take it or leave it.

items.sentence: Just do as I say.
items.translation: 照我说的做就行。
explanations: **do as I say** = 照我说的做。比 do what I say 略书面，语气偏权威。
近义：Do what I tell you / Follow my instructions。例句：Just do as I say and you'll be fine.

sentenceAudio.text: Just do as I say.

items.sentence: No more excuses.
items.translation: 别再找借口了。
explanations: **no more excuses** = 别再找借口。简短、终结性的表态，常出现在被反复爽约之后。
近义：Enough excuses / Stop making excuses。例句：No more excuses — I want the report by Friday.

sentenceAudio.text: No more excuses.

items.sentence: Do me a favor.
items.translation: 帮我个忙。
explanations: **do sb a favor** = 帮某人一个忙。请求帮助的万用句式，后面能直接接 to do 说明具体事。
近义：Give me a hand / Could you do me a favor? 例句：Do me a favor and keep an eye on my bag.

sentenceAudio.text: Do me a favor.

items.sentence: Who do you think you are?
items.translation: 你以为你是谁？
explanations: **Who do you think you are?** = 你以为你是谁？质问对方凭什么这么说话做事，是最常见的反击句。
近义：What gives you the right? 例句：Who do you think you are — talking to me like that?

sentenceAudio.text: Who do you think you are?

items.sentence: You'll be sorry if you do that.
items.translation: 你要是那么做会后悔的。
explanations: **You'll be sorry** = 你会后悔的。警告或威胁，语气轻重看场合；后接 if 从句说明后悔的缘由。
近义：You'll regret it。例句：You'll be sorry if you do that — I'm not joking.

sentenceAudio.text: You'll be sorry if you do that.

items.sentence: Drop the act — I know what you did.
items.translation: 别装了，我知道你干了什么。
explanations: **drop the act** = 别装了、收起那套。act 指装出来的样子，drop 有「撂下」的劲。
近义：Cut the act / Stop pretending。例句：Drop the act — I know what you did.

sentenceAudio.text: Drop the act — I know what you did.

items.sentence: What were you thinking?
items.translation: 你当时在想什么？
explanations: **What were you thinking?** = 你当时到底在想什么？事后追责的固定问法，暗示对方做了蠢事。
近义：What came over you? 例句：What were you thinking — driving after all that wine?

sentenceAudio.text: What were you thinking?

items.sentence: That's going too far.
items.translation: 这太过分了。
explanations: **go too far** = 做得过分、越界。too far 在这里指程度，不是距离。
近义：That crosses the line。例句：That's going too far — apologize right now.

sentenceAudio.text: That's going too far.

items.sentence: You've gone too far this time.
items.translation: 这次你太过分了。
explanations: **go too far** 用完成时 = 已经越界了，强调事情已经发生、收不回来。
区别：That's going too far 是就当下的事评价；You've gone too far 是直接给对方定性。例句：You've gone too far this time — don't call me again.

sentenceAudio.text: You've gone too far this time.

items.sentence: You're nothing to me.
items.translation: 你对我来说什么都不是。
hints: 你对我来说什么都不是。
explanations: **be nothing to sb** = 对某人来说无足轻重。关系彻底了断时的狠话。
近义：You mean nothing to me。例句：You're nothing to me now — don't ever call again.

sentenceAudio.text: You're nothing to me.

items.sentence: You set me up — it was a trap!
items.translation: 你陷害我，那是个圈套！

grammar.meaning: set sb up 陷害某人

explanations: **set sb up** = 陷害某人、给某人下套；也能表示「撮合两人交往」（set sb up with sb），看宾语判断。
近义：frame sb（伪造证据陷害）。例句：You set me up — it was a trap!

sentenceAudio.text: You set me up — it was a trap!

items.sentence: You're so careless — you left the door open.
items.translation: 你太粗心了，门都没关。
explanations: **careless** = 粗心的、不上心的。指责别人疏漏时的直接说法，语气比「笨」轻。
近义：You're so sloppy（更口语）。例句：You're so careless — you left the door wide open.

sentenceAudio.text: You're so careless — you left the door open.

items.sentence: Stop giving me a hard time.
items.translation: 别再为难我了。
explanations: **give sb a hard time** = 为难某人、找某人麻烦；也可指「让某人日子不好过」。
近义：Stop hassling me / Get off my back。例句：Stop giving me a hard time — I'm doing my best.

sentenceAudio.text: Stop giving me a hard time.

items.sentence: Stay out of it — this is between us.
items.translation: 别插手，这是我们之间的事。

grammar.meaning: stay out of it 别插手

explanations: **stay out of it** = 别插手、别搅进来。it 指正在发生的那件事，常配 between us 划清范围。
近义：Mind your own business / Don't get involved。例句：Stay out of it — this is between us.

sentenceAudio.text: Stay out of it — this is between us.

items.sentence: I won't put up with this anymore.
items.translation: 我不会再忍这件事了。
explanations: **put up with sth** = 忍受某事。put 与 up 中间不能插别的词，with 后接忍受的对象。
近义：tolerate / stand。例句：I won't put up with this anymore — one more word and I'm leaving.

sentenceAudio.text: I won't put up with this anymore.

items.sentence: What's the fuss about?
items.translation: 闹什么呢？
explanations: **fuss** = 大惊小怪、无谓的吵闹。What's the fuss about? 就是「至于这么大动静吗」。
近义：What's all the commotion? 例句：What's the fuss about — it's only a little rain.

sentenceAudio.text: What's the fuss about?

items.sentence: I'm not in a good mood.
items.translation: 我心情不太好。
chunks: I'm not in a good mood.
explanations: **in a good mood** = 心情好。加 not 就是「心情不好」，是英语里最常用的状态自述。
近义：I'm in a bad mood / I'm feeling down。例句：I'm not in a good mood — let's talk tomorrow.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm not in a good mood.

items.sentence: I'm cranky today.
items.translation: 我今天脾气不好。
explanations: **cranky** = 烦躁、爱发脾气的，多因没睡好或饿了。比 angry 轻，是美式口语常用词。
近义：I'm grumpy / I'm in a bad mood。例句：I'm cranky today — I didn't sleep well.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm cranky today.

items.sentence: Leave me alone.
items.translation: 让我一个人待着。

grammar.meaning: leave sb alone 别烦某人

explanations: **leave sb alone** = 别打扰某人、让某人静静。比 go away 温和，重点在「别烦我」。
近义：Give me some space / Back off。例句：Leave me alone — I need to think.

sentenceAudio.text: Leave me alone.

items.sentence: Why the long face?
items.translation: 怎么愁眉苦脸的？

grammar.meaning: long face 拉长的脸、不高兴

explanations: **long face** = 拉长的脸，指不高兴的表情。Why the long face? 是省略句，等于 Why do you have a long face?。
近义：What's got you down? 例句：Why the long face — did your team lose again?

sentenceAudio.text: Why the long face?

items.sentence: That's ridiculous.
items.translation: 这太荒唐了。
explanations: **ridiculous** = 荒唐的、离谱的。表达强烈不认同，比 silly 重、比 absurd 日常。
近义：That's absurd / That's insane（更口语）。例句：That's ridiculous — nobody would believe it.

sentenceAudio.text: That's ridiculous.

items.sentence: That's more like it.
items.translation: 这才像话。
explanations: **more like it** = 这才像话、这才对嘛。对刚出现的好转表示认可。
近义：Now you're talking / That's better。例句：That's more like it — now we're getting somewhere.

sentenceAudio.text: That's more like it.

items.sentence: I hope your idea takes wings.
items.translation: 希望你的想法能顺利实现。

grammar.meaning: take wings 腾飞、取得进展

explanations: **take wings** = 展翅高飞，比喻想法、计划腾飞起来。祝福或期待时用。
近义：I hope it takes off。例句：I hope your idea takes wings — it deserves a chance.

sentenceAudio.text: I hope your idea takes wings.

items.sentence: Don't rob Peter to pay Paul.
items.translation: 别拆东墙补西墙。
chunks: Don't rob Peter to pay Paul.

grammar.meaning: rob Peter to pay Paul 拆东墙补西墙

explanations: **rob Peter to pay Paul** = 拆东墙补西墙，借新债还旧债。Peter 和 Paul 在英语里泛指「张三李四」。
近义：take from one to give to another。例句：Don't rob Peter to pay Paul — fix the real problem.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't rob Peter to pay Paul.

items.sentence: I almost made it.
items.translation: 我差一点就成了。
explanations: **make it** = 成功、赶上、撑过来（看语境）。almost made it 就是「差一点点就做到了」。
近义：I was so close。例句：I almost made it — the train doors shut right in front of me.

sentenceAudio.text: I almost made it.

items.sentence: I don't have the heart to tell her.
items.translation: 我不忍心告诉她。
explanations: **have the heart to do sth** = 忍心做某事。多用于否定，表示「狠不下心」。
近义：I can't bring myself to tell her。例句：I don't have the heart to tell her the cat is gone.

sentenceAudio.text: I don't have the heart to tell her.

items.sentence: I can't bear to watch.
items.translation: 我不忍心看下去。
explanations: **can't bear to do sth** = 不忍心做某事、受不了做某事。bear 在这里是「忍受」。
近义：I can't stand to watch。例句：I can't bear to watch — tell me how it ends.

sentenceAudio.text: I can't bear to watch.

items.sentence: A word of advice — book your tickets early.
items.translation: 给你个忠告，早点订票。
explanations: **A word of advice** = 给你个忠告。在给出建议前先提个醒，比直接说 Listen to me 柔和，常用于朋友之间。
近义：Here's a tip / A piece of advice. 例句：A word of advice — never sign anything without reading it twice.

sentenceAudio.text: A word of advice — book your tickets early.

items.sentence: Take it from me — the exam is easier than you think.
items.translation: 听我的没错，考试比你想的简单。
chunks: the exam is easier than you think.
explanations: **Take it from me** = 听我的没错。用自己的亲身经历给对方打保票，语气亲近且有分量。
近义：Trust me on this. 例句：Take it from me — you'll regret quitting without a plan.

sentenceAudio.text: Take it from me — the exam is easier than you think.

items.sentence: Be that as it may, we still need to finish today.
items.translation: 即便如此，今天还是得完成。
chunks: we still need to finish today.
explanations: **Be that as it may** = 即便如此。先承认对方说得有道理，再转折说出自己的重点，是正式场合好用的让步句。
近义：Even so / That said. 例句：Be that as it may, the deadline hasn't changed.

sentenceAudio.text: Be that as it may, we still need to finish today.

items.sentence: Let's play it by ear and see how the weather is.
items.translation: 随机应变吧，看天气再定。
chunks: and see how the weather is.
explanations: **Play it by ear** = 随机应变、走一步看一步。原指不看谱凭耳朵演奏，引申为不提前定死计划。
近义：See how it goes. 例句：Let's not book anything — we'll play it by ear.

sentenceAudio.text: Let's play it by ear and see how the weather is.

items.sentence: Anything you say — you're the boss here.
items.translation: 听你的，这儿你说了算。
explanations: **Anything you say** = 听你的、照你说的办。表示完全服从对方，语气可诚恳也可带点无奈。
近义：Whatever you say / Your call. 例句：Anything you say — I'll follow your lead.

sentenceAudio.text: Anything you say — you're the boss here.

items.sentence: I suppose so, though I'm not really sure.
items.translation: 我想是吧，虽然不太确定。
explanations: **I suppose so** = 我想是吧。勉强的同意，暗示自己并不十分认同，只是不想争。
对比：I think so 更有把握；I suppose so 把握不足。例句：I suppose so, but don't quote me on it.

sentenceAudio.text: I suppose so, though I'm not really sure.

items.sentence: I'm not sure — let me check and get back to you.
items.translation: 我不确定，我查一下再回复你。
chunks: let me check and get back to you.
explanations: **I'm not sure** = 我不确定。职场里最安全的缓冲句，比直接说 No 或 I don't know 更专业。
搭配：get back to you 稍后答复你。例句：I'm not sure — let me check with the team and get back to you.

sentenceAudio.text: I'm not sure — let me check and get back to you.

items.sentence: Do you have a problem with the new plan?
items.translation: 你对新方案有意见吗？
chunks: a problem with the new plan?

grammar.pos: 助动词 + 主语 + 动词

explanations: **Have a problem with sth** = 对某事有意见、有不满。可直接询问，也可反击别人。
注意语气：问句是询问；陈述句 I have a problem with that. 就是明确反对了。例句：Do you have a problem with the way I did it?

sentenceAudio.text: Do you have a problem with the new plan?

items.sentence: You helped me last week, so now we are even.
items.translation: 你上周帮过我，现在咱俩扯平了。
explanations: **We are even** = 咱俩扯平了。指人情、账目两清，谁也不欠谁，常带轻松口吻。
近义：We're square / Call it even. 例句：Thanks for the ride — now we're even.

sentenceAudio.text: You helped me last week, so now we are even.

items.sentence: Fine, have your way — but don't blame me later.
items.translation: 行，随你，但回头别怪我。
explanations: **Have your way** = 随你、由着你的意思来。多带无奈或不满，暗示后果自负。
近义：Have it your way. 例句：Fine, have your way — just don't come crying to me.

sentenceAudio.text: Fine, have your way — but don't blame me later.

items.sentence: Don't be mad at me — it was an honest mistake.
items.translation: 别生我气，这是个无心的错。
explanations: **Be mad at sb** = 生某人的气。加上 an honest mistake（无心的过失）就是在请求原谅。
近义：Don't be angry with me. 例句：Don't be mad at me — the file got deleted by accident.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't be mad at me — it was an honest mistake.

items.sentence: Do I have to go to the meeting — I'm exhausted.
items.translation: 我一定得去开会吗，我累坏了。
chunks: Do I have to go to the meeting —
explanations: **Do I have to...?** = 我非得……吗？带委屈或不情愿的抱怨口气，比 Must I 更口语。
近义：Is it really necessary? 例句：Do I have to stay late again — I've got plans.

sentenceAudio.text: Do I have to go to the meeting — I'm exhausted.

items.sentence: You go girl — show them what you can do!
items.translation: 加油姑娘，让他们看看你的本事。
chunks: show them what you can do!
explanations: **You go girl!** = 加油姑娘！专门给女性打气的口头语，热情、带姐妹感，多用于朋友之间。
近义：Go for it / You got this. 例句：You go girl — that presentation was amazing!

sentenceAudio.text: You go girl — show them what you can do!

items.sentence: By the way, did you get my message?
items.translation: 顺便问一下，你收到我的消息了吗？
explanations: **By the way**（缩写 BTW）= 顺便说一下。用来插入一个跟当前话题无关的新话题。
近义：Incidentally / Speaking of which. 例句：By the way, the meeting moved to three.

sentenceAudio.text: By the way, did you get my message?

items.sentence: Hey, what's happening — long time no see!
items.translation: 嘿，最近怎么样，好久不见。
explanations: **What's happening?** = 最近怎么样、有什么新鲜事？轻松的朋友式问候，比 How are you 更随意。
近义：What's up / How's it going. 例句：Hey man, what's happening — you look great!

sentenceAudio.text: Hey, what's happening — long time no see!

items.sentence: How's everything at your new job?
items.translation: 你的新工作一切都好吗？
explanations: **How's everything?** = 一切都好吗？泛问近况的问候，比 How are you 更关心具体生活状态。
近义：How are things? 例句：How's everything at home — is your mother better?

sentenceAudio.text: How's everything at your new job?

items.sentence: Make yourself comfortable and feel at home.
items.translation: 别拘束，就当在自己家一样。
explanations: **Feel at home** = 像在自己家一样自在。招待客人时的标准客套话，等于「别客气」。
近义：Make yourself at home. 例句：Come in, feel at home — I'll get you a drink.

sentenceAudio.text: Make yourself comfortable and feel at home.

items.sentence: Could I get a little help with these boxes?
items.translation: 能帮我搬一下这些箱子吗？
chunks: Could I get a little help
explanations: **A little help** = 帮个小忙。用 little 把请求说小，显得不麻烦别人，比 Can you help me 更客气。
近义：Could you give me a hand? 例句：A little help here — this thing weighs a ton.

sentenceAudio.text: Could I get a little help with these boxes?

items.sentence: No matter what happens, my heart belongs to you.
items.translation: 不管发生什么，我的心都属于你。
explanations: **My heart belongs to you** = 我的心属于你。很重的一句表白，belong to 是「归属于」，比 I love you 更庄重。
近义：I'm yours. 例句：No matter how far apart we are, my heart belongs to you.

sentenceAudio.text: No matter what happens, my heart belongs to you.

items.sentence: Why don't you take the lead on this one?
items.translation: 这件事你来牵头吧。
chunks: Why don't you take the lead
explanations: **Take the lead** = 牵头、带头、挑大梁。用 Why don't you... 提建议，语气委婉不生硬。
近义：Lead the way / Head it up. 例句：You know the client best, so take the lead on this one.

sentenceAudio.text: Why don't you take the lead on this one?

items.sentence: I dropped the ball on the last order — sorry.
items.translation: 上一单我搞砸了，抱歉。
explanations: **Drop the ball** = 掉链子、把事情办砸了。源自运动里没接住球，职场里用来认错最常用。
近义：Screw up / Mess up. 例句：Sorry, I dropped the ball on the invoice — I'll fix it today.

sentenceAudio.text: I dropped the ball on the last order — sorry.

items.sentence: Go big or go home — this is your only chance.
items.translation: 要么全力以赴，要么别干——这可是你唯一的机会。
hints: 要么全力以赴，要么别干

grammar.meaning: 要么全力以赴，要么别做

explanations: **Go big or go home** = 要么干票大的，要么干脆别干。强调不留后路、全力投入的拼劲。
近义：All in. 例句：We're pitching to the biggest client — go big or go home.

sentenceAudio.text: Go big or go home — this is your only chance.

items.sentence: Please come in one at a time, not all together.
items.translation: 请一个一个进来，别一起挤。
chunks: Please come in one at a time,
explanations: **One at a time** = 一次一个、一个一个来。维持秩序时的标准说法，常搭配 please 使用。
近义：One by one. 例句：One at a time, please — the elevator is small.

sentenceAudio.text: Please come in one at a time, not all together.

items.sentence: I'll try my best, but I can't promise anything.
items.translation: 我会尽力，但不能保证什么。
explanations: **Try my best** = 尽我所能。比 I'll try 更认真；后面加 but I can't promise 就是先把预期压住。
对比：do my best 更侧重「尽力做」；try my best 侧重「尝试」。例句：I'll try my best — no promises though.

sentenceAudio.text: I'll try my best, but I can't promise anything.

items.sentence: Be ready for anything — the plan may change.
items.translation: 做好万全准备，计划可能变。

grammar.meaning: 对任何情况都做好准备

explanations: **Be ready for sth** = 为某事做好准备。加 anything 就是「什么情况都可能，都得有准备」。
近义：Expect the unexpected. 例句：Be ready for anything — the client loves changing specs.

sentenceAudio.text: Be ready for anything — the plan may change.

items.sentence: Could you speed up a little — we're running late.
items.translation: 你能快点吗，我们要迟到了。
chunks: Could you speed up a little —
explanations: **Speed up** = 加快速度。反义是 slow down；加 a little 让催促听起来不那么冲。
近义：Hurry up / Step on it. 例句：Could you speed up a bit — the train leaves at six.

sentenceAudio.text: Could you speed up a little — we're running late.

items.sentence: Could you back up a little — you're blocking the door.
items.translation: 你能退后一点吗，你挡住门了。
chunks: Could you back up a little —
explanations: **Back up** = 后退（空间）；同一短语另有「支持」和「备份」两义，靠语境区分。
近义：Step back / Move back. 例句：Back up — you're standing too close to the edge.

sentenceAudio.text: Could you back up a little — you're blocking the door.

items.sentence: Drink some water and sober up before you leave.
items.translation: 喝点水，醒醒酒再走。
chunks: and sober up before you leave.
explanations: **Sober up** = 醒酒、清醒过来。sober 本身是形容词「清醒的」，加 up 变成「从醉态里出来」。
近义：Sleep it off. 例句：He needs an hour to sober up before he can drive.

sentenceAudio.text: Drink some water and sober up before you leave.

items.sentence: We strive to make every customer feel welcome.
items.translation: 我们努力让每位顾客感到宾至如归。
hints: 让每位顾客感到宾至如归
explanations: **Strive to do sth** = 力求、努力做某事。比 try hard 更书面、更有使命感，企业文案和演讲高频。
近义：Endeavor to. 例句：We strive to improve our service every single day.

sentenceAudio.text: We strive to make every customer feel welcome.

items.sentence: The moment the alarm rang, the crew sprang into action.
items.translation: 警报一响，全组人立刻行动起来。
explanations: **Spring into action** = 立刻行动起来。spring 是「像弹簧一样弹起」，过去式 sprang，画面感强。
近义：Jump into action. 例句：Emergency teams sprang into action right after the quake.

sentenceAudio.text: The moment the alarm rang, the crew sprang into action.

items.sentence: Don't be too hard on yourself — tomorrow is another day.
items.translation: 别太苛责自己，明天又是新的一天。
chunks: Don't be too hard on yourself —
explanations: **Tomorrow is another day** = 明天又是新的一天。《乱世佳人》结尾名句，用来安慰人翻篇、别纠结当下。
近义：There's always tomorrow. 例句：We lost this one, but tomorrow is another day.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't be too hard on yourself — tomorrow is another day.

items.sentence: Don't let the grass grow under your feet — apply now.
items.translation: 别让机会从脚下溜走，现在就申请。
chunks: Don't let the grass grow under your feet —
explanations: **Don't let the grass grow under your feet** = 别磨蹭、趁热打铁。画面是人在原地站太久，脚下都长草了。
近义：Strike while the iron is hot. 例句：Don't let the grass grow under your feet — the offer expires Friday.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't let the grass grow under your feet — apply now.

items.sentence: He was on his knees, begging for a second chance.
items.translation: 他跪了下来，乞求第二次机会。
explanations: **On one's knees** = 跪下、跪着。字面跪地乞求；引申义是「濒临崩溃」（The company was on its knees.）。
近义：Beg and plead. 例句：She was on her knees scrubbing the floor all morning.

sentenceAudio.text: He was on his knees, begging for a second chance.

items.sentence: Get down from there — you'll hurt yourself.
items.translation: 快下来，你会伤到自己的。
explanations: **Get down** = 下来（从高处）。注意别和「趴下」的 Get down!（危险时喊的）搞混——那个靠语气和场景区分。
近义：Come down. 例句：Get down from the ladder — I'll hold it steady.

sentenceAudio.text: Get down from there — you'll hurt yourself.

items.sentence: It's getting late — let me walk you out.
items.translation: 天色晚了，我送你出去。
explanations: **Walk you out** = 送你出去（陪走到门口或车边）。待客、约会结束时都常用，比 goodbye 多一分周到。
近义：See you to the door. 例句：Stay a while — I'll walk you out whenever you're ready.

sentenceAudio.text: It's getting late — let me walk you out.

items.sentence: It's midnight — how are you gonna get home?
items.translation: 都半夜了，你打算怎么回家？
chunks: how are you gonna get home?
explanations: **How are you gonna...?** = 你打算怎么……？gonna 是 going to 的口语缩写，这句话是关心对方的安排。
近义：How will you get back? 例句：The buses stopped running — how are you gonna get home?

sentenceAudio.text: It's midnight — how are you gonna get home?

items.sentence: He worked his way through college by washing dishes.
items.translation: 他靠洗碗打工读完了大学。
chunks: He worked his way through college
hints: 他一路打工读完了大学
explanations: **Work one's way (through)** = 靠打工、一步一步奋斗着完成。强调过程辛苦但没有外援。
近义：Put oneself through school. 例句：She worked her way up from intern to manager.

sentenceAudio.text: He worked his way through college by washing dishes.

items.sentence: I'm working — get out of my face!
items.translation: 我在工作——别来烦我！
explanations: **Get out of my face** = 别在我眼前晃、滚远点。字面是「从我脸前消失」，比 Get lost 更冲，多用于被反复打扰时。
近义：Get out of my sight / Back off. 例句：I'm on a deadline — get out of my face!

sentenceAudio.text: I'm working — get out of my face!

items.sentence: Don't suck up to the boss — just do your job.
items.translation: 别拍老板马屁——把自己的活干好就行。
chunks: Don't suck up to the boss —
explanations: **Suck up to sb** = 拍某人马屁、谄媚讨好。名词形式 **suck-up** 就是「马屁精」。
近义：Butter sb up / Kiss up to sb. 例句：He's always sucking up to the manager.

sentenceAudio.text: Don't suck up to the boss — just do your job.

items.sentence: He got loaded at the party and couldn't drive home.
items.translation: 他在聚会上喝大了，没法开车回家。
chunks: He got loaded at the party
explanations: **Get loaded** = 喝醉（美式俚语）。load 本义「装载」，引申成把人「灌满酒」，比 get drunk 更随意。
近义：Get wasted / Tie one on. 例句：They got loaded and sang all night.

sentenceAudio.text: He got loaded at the party and couldn't drive home.

items.sentence: Your guess was spot on — it turned out exactly right.
items.translation: 你猜得完全正确——结果一点不差。
explanations: **Spot on** = 完全正确、正中要害。英式口语常用，比 exactly right 更地道、更轻快。
近义：Right on the money / Bang on. 例句：Your summary of the case was spot on.

sentenceAudio.text: Your guess was spot on — it turned out exactly right.

items.sentence: We can meet at eight — that is fine by me.
items.translation: 我们八点见——我没意见。
explanations: **Fine by me** = 我没意见、我无所谓。用于爽快答应别人的安排，语气随和。
近义：Works for me / I am good with that. 例句：Take the later flight — that is fine by me.

sentenceAudio.text: We can meet at eight — that is fine by me.

items.sentence: Count me in — I am on board with the plan.
items.translation: 算我一个——我同意这个计划。
chunks: I am on board with the plan.
explanations: **On board** 字面「在船上」，引申为「同意、加入、支持某个计划」。I am on board = 我加入、我赞成。
近义：I am in / Count me in / I am game. 例句：If everyone is on board, we will start next week.

sentenceAudio.text: Count me in — I am on board with the plan.

items.sentence: Here goes — I am going to ask her out.
items.translation: 豁出去了——我这就去约她。
chunks: I am going to ask her out.
explanations: **Here goes** 是「要开始了、豁出去了」的感叹，常在鼓足勇气做某件事前说，比如跳伞、表白、上台演讲。
近义：Here we go / Wish me luck. 例句：Here goes — fingers crossed!

sentenceAudio.text: Here goes — I am going to ask her out.

items.sentence: Play nice with your little brother.
items.translation: 跟你弟弟好好相处。
chunks: Play nice with your little brother.
explanations: **Play nice** = 友好相处、别闹。多对孩子说，也可以调侃成年人之间「别斗了」。
近义：Be nice / Get along. 例句：Play nice, kids — no pushing.

sentenceAudio.text: Play nice with your little brother.

items.sentence: Scoot over — I need a seat too.
items.translation: 挪过去点——我也要坐。
explanations: **Scoot over** = 往旁边挪一点，给别人腾个位置。scoot 本义是「快速滑动」，口语里就是「挪挪屁股」。
近义：Move over / Slide over / Budge up. 例句：Scoot over so I can sit down.

sentenceAudio.text: Scoot over — I need a seat too.

items.sentence: Hold on — put him on, please.
items.translation: 等一下——请让他接电话。
explanations: **Put sb on**（打电话）= 让某人来接电话。Put him on 就是「把他接进来」。
反义：Take a message（代为留言）. 例句：Is Sarah there? Put her on, please.

sentenceAudio.text: Hold on — put him on, please.

items.sentence: The movie was sweet, if a little cheesy.
items.translation: 那部电影挺温馨，就是有点俗套。
explanations: **Cheesy** = 俗套、煽情得让人有点尴尬。a little cheesy = 有点俗，贬中带夸。
近义：Corny / Cliché / Tacky. 例句：His pickup line was a little cheesy.

sentenceAudio.text: The movie was sweet, if a little cheesy.

items.sentence: Do not tell the neighbors — they are so nosy.
items.translation: 别告诉邻居——他们太好打听了。
explanations: **Nosy** = 爱打听、好管闲事，比 curious 带明显的贬义，形容总爱探听别人隐私的人。
近义：Snoopy / Have a big mouth. 例句：Our neighbor is so nosy about our plans.

sentenceAudio.text: Do not tell the neighbors — they are so nosy.

items.sentence: Try the dessert — you are in for a treat.
items.translation: 尝尝这甜点——你有口福了。
chunks: you are in for a treat.
explanations: **In for a treat** = 有好东西等着你、有得享受了。常用在推荐美食、演出、电影之前。
近义：You will love it / You are in for a surprise. 例句：Wait till you hear her sing — you are in for a treat.

sentenceAudio.text: Try the dessert — you are in for a treat.

items.sentence: For real — you actually won the lottery?
items.translation: 真的假的——你真中彩票了？
explanations: **For real** = 真的假的、当真？既可表惊讶反问，也可以作「说真的」用。
近义：Seriously? / No way! / For real though（说真的）. 例句：For real, you are moving to Japan?

sentenceAudio.text: For real — you actually won the lottery?
